result:
Two patient chart files call `useAbortController` directly, and both would be affected by a change in its behaviour:

1. **Vitals & biometrics form**: `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/exported-vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx`. The controller is created at line 87 and passed to `createOrUpdateVitalsAndBiometrics` in the save handler `savePatientVitalsAndBiometrics` (lines 180–272, usages at 231 and 267).

2. **Lab results form**: `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/lab-results/exported-lab-results-form.workspace.tsx`. The controller is created at line 70 and used in the submit handler (lines 245–361) for `fetchSavedLabResults` (254), `completeOrderWithSavedResults` (304) and `updateOrderResult` (338). I did not confirm where the handler's declaration starts, so 245 is the first line I saw it using the controller.

The hook itself is in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useAbortController.ts` (lines 25–38). It returns a fresh controller when the current one is aborted, and aborts it on unmount. Any change to that contract would change how both forms cancel in-flight requests when the workspace closes or unmounts.

Indirect exposure is wider than these two files. `useOpenmrsSWR` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useOpenmrsSWR.ts`, lines 70–87) calls `useAbortController` internally, so every chart data hook built on `useOpenmrsSWR` inherits the behaviour. I did not enumerate those consumers. The laboratory app also uses the hook, but it is outside the patient chart. The Falkon grep reported 29 matches across the core repo, and the laboratory app had 6.
